title: Social Security Legislation Amendment (Disaster Recovery Allowance) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would establish a Disaster Recovery Allowance providing temporary income support to eligible people who lose income because of disasters occurring within Australia.
It would provide fortnightly payments for up to 13 weeks, with maximum rates linked to Newstart Allowance or Youth Allowance and detailed eligibility rules.
From 1 October 2013, the Minister could activate payments for nationally significant disasters, specifying affected areas or industries within areas, subject to statutory criteria.
changes: The allowance would be taxable income and included in the Beneficiary Tax Offset scheme.
People already receiving specified social security entitlements or other excluded payments would be ineligible.
Payments would be unavailable where an assurance of support is in force.
Claims would generally be due within six months of a disaster determination, with extensions for qualifying special circumstances.
Receipt would not automatically confer other benefits available to recipients of social security payments.
summary.affected: Australian residents and specified visa holders meeting the age, income-loss and other eligibility requirements are affected.

speeches.speaker: Michael Keenan
speeches.brief: Supported the Social Security Legislation Amendment (Disaster Recovery Allowance) Bill 2013, which would replace the disaster income recovery subsidy with a 13-week payment from 1 October this year; outlined a proposal for small businesses to access loans up to $100,000 at four per cent for up to seven years, plus tax relief.

speeches.speaker: Graham Perrett
speeches.brief: Supported the Disaster Recovery Allowance bill and questioned the proposed small-business commitment of up to $100,000 loans at four per cent, citing disaster impacts in Queensland and seeking details of offsets for the financial commitment.

speeches.speaker: Shayne Neumann
speeches.brief: Announced that the Disaster Recovery Allowance would replace the ex gratia Disaster Income Recovery Subsidy, providing legislated support with clear eligibility, activation, review, fraud and debt-recovery processes for people whose incomes are affected by fire, cyclone or flood, with preparatory work targeted for the 2013-14 summer.
